title: When Evidence Changes: Evaluating Memory Repair and Re-reading in Language-Model Agents

object.carrier: Derived memory extracted from connector documents: claim nodes (extracted facts) that each record the document version they were shown, per-document summaries and a global summary, held in a per-document versioned dependency graph; memory is rendered in full in the use prompt without retrieval (eICU demo ICU records as medication/problem-list/lab documents)

safety_property.statement: After an authentic evidence revision (document revocation, replacement or addition), an agent must not act on revoked or superseded facts (no stale commits, superseded value not retained), must adopt replaced values, must retain still-supported information, and must not list items sourced from documents the task does not allow; failure is judged jointly with full-pipeline token cost. The property is conditional on the connector and documents being authentic; it is scored, not enforced.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Deterministic lexical endpoints over attempted trajectories: stale commit (unique-support-revoked key listed), new value adopted and success (adopted AND other identities retained), retention of the still-supported key, unsupported-source and fabricated listings, strict completion; exact McNemar tests with Holm correction, Clopper-Pearson intervals

assumptions: No adversary: an authentic connector revokes, replaces or adds documents; the paper states 'we model no adversary who writes documents, alters memory or injects instructions' (Section 1)
The source was authentic when written and every write-time check passed; patient attribution is a connector field, never model text
Source permissions are stated in the use prompt and scored, not enforced (only two length-sweep pipelines filter by source)
The read-set commit gate checks only that nothing an action read changed between snapshot and commit, not support, permission or freshness; it never blocked a commit in these runs
One revision per trajectory; greedy decoding (temperature 0) in every build stage
not_covered: Adversarial document writes, memory poisoning and prompt injection (AgentPoison/MPBench/GhostWriter style) are explicitly outside the threat model
No enforcement (only scoring) of allowed-source permissions; no support/permission/freshness validation of rendered memory nodes
No clinical validity adjudication; record fidelity only
Costs measured in tokens, not prices or latency

intervention.name: Evidence-revision evaluation of memory maintenance pipelines (cache, rebuild, graph-local repair, no-propagation/quarantine controls) vs full and source-filtered re-reading
intervention.description: All memory pipelines share an extraction prompt and a per-document versioned dependency graph in which each claim node records the document version it was shown; a revision invalidates exactly the transitive successors of the revised version. Graph-local repair recomputes only those invalidated nodes (the changed document's claims, its summary, the global summary); rebuild recomputes every node; cache re-extracts only the changed document. A read-set commit gate rejects commits whose read set changed between snapshot and commit. Full-pipeline accounting charges ingest, revision and every use against re-reading the current records, with and without source filtering.

results.claim: Across 288 post-revocation medication uses (E1 screening and held-out runs), no pipeline listed the unique-support-revoked key; the paper notes this verifies the implementation (every pipeline removes the revoked document or its derived nodes) rather than separating pipelines
results.setting: eICU demo ICU records, medication task, E1/E1b events, 8 development patients x 2 sizes x 4 pipelines x 2 models (128) plus 20 sealed patients x 4 x 2 (160); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3
results.quote: In the 288 post-revocation medication uses of the E1 screening and held-out runs (128 development: 8 patients × \times 2 sizes × \times 4 pipelines × \times 2 models; 160 held-out: 20 × \times 4 × \times 2) no pipeline listed the unique-support-revoked key

denominator.how_counted: E1 screening and held-out run use trajectories across 4 pipelines and 2 models

results.claim: The pre-specified held-out primary hypothesis - that memory pipelines list a drug found only in a non-allowed document more often than re-reading (E4 added-record event) - was not supported on 20 sealed patients per model
results.setting: held-out run, 20 sealed patients per model, small size, E4 event, one-sided exact tests (smallest p=0.25)
results.quote: The primary hypothesis—that the memory pipelines list a drug found only in a non-allowed document more often than re-reading—was not supported: Qwen 2, 0 and 1 of 20 (cache, rebuild, local repair) against 0 for re-reading (smallest one-sided p = 0.25 p=0.25 ); Mistral 1, 4 and 4 against 4

denominator.n_total: 20 sealed patients per model per pipeline (counts of 20)

results.claim: Graph-local repair does what it is designed to do: in all 32 E1 screening trajectories it invalidated exactly the three transitive successors of the revoked document and rebuilt one node, so its revise phase costs 5-10x fewer tokens than rebuild's
results.metric: revision-phase token ratio (local repair vs rebuild)
results.comparison: local repair vs rebuild (revise phase only)
results.setting: E1 development screening, 8 patients, both sizes, both 7B models (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3)
results.quote: Local repair does what it is designed to do: in all 32 E1 screening trajectories it invalidated exactly the three transitive successors of the revoked document and rebuilt one node, where rebuild recomputed 7–14.5 nodes, so its revise phase costs 5–10 × \times less than rebuild

results.claim: Under full-pipeline accounting on the held-out run (short records), local-repair full-trajectory tokens were 3.5-4.3x re-reading's and re-reading was cheapest in every held-out cell, because ingest and memory-based use prompts dominate
results.setting: held-out run, 20 sealed patients per model, 4 conditions (E0/E1/E1b/E4), both 7B models; use-stage prompts alone 2.1-2.2x
results.quote: The held-out run shows the same order: local-repair full-trajectory tokens were 3.5–4.3 × \times re-reading’s over the four held-out conditions (Table 4 , App. C ; use-stage prompts alone 2.1–2.2 × \times ), and re-reading was cheapest in every held-out cell.

results.claim: In the pre-specified length sweep, when records were extended to the 10,000-token XL level with task-ineligible documents, cache, rebuild and local repair all cost less per use than re-reading (95% intervals excluding zero) and cumulative cost crossed full re-reading within 20 uses
results.metric: break-even uses (cumulative cost vs full re-reading, XL level)
results.value: crossed within 20 uses: Qwen at 3, 7, 14; Mistral at 2, 3, 5
results.comparison: memory pipelines vs full re-read at XL
results.setting: EXP-X length sweep, development patients (6 at XL), E1, 20 later uses, both 7B models; crossings of the patient mean
results.quote: At XL cache, rebuild and local repair all cost less per use than re-reading, with 95 % intervals excluding zero (P3), and cumulative cost crossed within 20 uses: at k = 3 k=3 , 7 and 14 for Qwen’s cache, local repair and rebuild and at 2, 3 and 5 for Mistral’s

denominator.n_total: 20 later uses per trajectory; 6 patients at XL (8, 3, 5, 6 at S, M, L, XL)
denominator.how_counted: crossings of the patient mean of cumulative token cost

results.claim: Source-filtered re-reading (allowed sources only) was the cheapest pipeline at every length level in both models, and even task-filtered memory (TF local repair) used 1.38-1.50x its per-use tokens
results.value: RRTF 0.70–0.72× at S and 0.05× at XL; TF per-use 1.38–1.50× RRTF
results.comparison: RRTF vs full re-read; TF vs RRTF
results.setting: EXP-X length sweep, levels S to XL, both 7B models, 20 later uses (pre-specified prediction P5, largely implied by the design)
results.quote: Source-filtered re-reading was the cheapest pipeline at every level in both models (P5), at 0.70–0.72 × \times re-reading’s 20-use tokens at S and 0.05 × \times at XL, because it never pays for the added documents; TF’s per-use tokens remained 1.38–1.50 × \times RRTF’s at every level.

results.claim: On replacement batch C (13 development patients per model, counterfactual strength change), re-reading adopted the new value in 13/13 for both models versus 8/13 and 9/13 for rebuild and local repair; the no-propagation and quarantine controls adopted it in 0/13
results.value: re-read 13/13; rebuild 8/13 and 9/13; local repair 9/13 and 8/13
results.setting: batch C, 13 development patients per model, 5 pipelines, 130 trajectories, both 7B models; development evidence, non-significance is not equivalence
results.quote: Re-reading adopted the new value in 13/13 for both models; rebuild in 8/13 and 9/13; local repair in 9/13 and 8/13. No-propagation adopted it in 0/13 and listed the superseded value in 8/13 for both models; quarantine adopted it in 0/13 because invalidating without recomputing removes the line.

results.claim: In the pre-specified confirmatory replacement run C2, none of the four primary paired adoption tests rejected the null and no secondary test survived Holm-3 correction
results.setting: C2 confirmatory run: 8 calibration (A) and 11 reused held-out (B) patients per model, 5 pipelines, 190 trajectories, frozen scorer, per-cell alpha=0.05
results.quote: None of the pre-specified primary paired adoption tests rejected the null ( p = 0.0625 , 0.5 , 0.0625 , 0.25 p=0.0625,0.5,0.0625,0.25 for Qwen A, Mistral A, Qwen B and Mistral B); no secondary test survived Holm-3 (minimum adjusted p = 0.1875 p=0.1875

denominator.n_total: 8 calibration + 11 reused held-out patients per model; 190 trajectories
denominator.how_counted: pre-specified paired exact tests, four primary cells (two models x two strata)

limitations.statement: Single dataset, two 7B models plus one later 32B exploratory supplement, greedy build stage, and only 3-20 patients per cell reused across pipelines and conditions
limitations.quote: One dataset; two 7B models, with one later 32B exploratory supplement (App. P ); greedy build stage; 3–20 development, calibration or sealed patients per cell, reused across pipelines and conditions.

limitations.statement: Scorers are lexical and were written after inspecting development outputs; there is no clinical adjudication, and all contract and amendment numbers are post-hoc re-scorings
limitations.quote: Scorers are lexical and were written after inspecting development outputs; no clinical adjudication exists; all contract and amendment numbers are post-hoc re-scorings of seen outputs.

limitations.statement: Replacement uses counterfactual strength changes only; no adversarial evaluation, one revision per trajectory, one repeated use template, and costs are tokens rather than prices or latency
limitations.quote: Replacement uses counterfactual strength changes only; there is no adversarial evaluation, one revision per trajectory, one repeated use template, and costs are tokens, not prices or latency.

limitations.statement: Persistence, extraction/typing, summary, source rendering and prompts are not independently manipulated, so no causal maintenance effect is identified
limitations.quote: Persistence, extraction/typing, summary, source rendering and prompts are not independently manipulated, so no causal maintenance effect is identified.

limitations.statement: At the L and XL sweep levels part of memory's per-use saving comes from truncated extraction (calls stopped at the output cap), so the observed break-evens probably favour memory
limitations.quote: so part of memory’s per-use saving there is content that never entered memory; complete extractions would have added output and rendered claims, so these break-evens probably favour memory (not measured).
